actors: Professor Stuart Gietel-Basten (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
key_facts: Official data released in the last week show the ratio of China's dependent elderly people to the working-age population rose to 23% last year, overtaking the child dependency figure of 22%.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics, there are more than 223 million people aged 65 and above in China (nearly 16% of the total population) and about 213 million children aged 14 and under.

The ageing shift could add strain to pension, healthcare and long-term care systems; the one-child policy (1980 to end-2015) and rising living costs, changing gender roles and higher education levels have contributed to low birth rates.
More than 53 million elderly people were receiving senior citizen allowances and subsidies by the end of 2025, according to official figures.
importance_reason: Structural demographic milestone with long-run fiscal and growth implications for the world's second-largest economy, but no immediate market-moving event.
market_link: Shrinking workforce and rising pension/healthcare spending could weigh on China's long-term growth, consumption and fiscal balances, with indirect implications for global growth and demand-sensitive assets.

key_facts: Delivery drones operated by Amazon and Walmart are becoming part of everyday life in the US; Amazon Prime Air is expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns and has launched in and around Darlington, north England.

Residents describe the drone noise as an annoying buzz; acoustic researcher Antonio Torija Martinez (University of Salford) says drone sound is particularly noticeable even at low overall levels, and complaints are expected to grow as the sector expands.

The FAA regulates commercial drones in the US but has faced criticism for allowing noisy delivery operations; it says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for community concerns.

Startups are developing quieter designs: Greenjets claims its enclosed-propeller propulsion system can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds; Sharrow Engineering has developed tipless, loop-shaped propellers; Amazon says its latest propellers produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation.
importance_reason: Feature-level consumer/technology story about drone noise without direct market-moving effect.
